construction_markdown:
Fix \(K=\mathbb F_2[u]/(u^8+u^4+u^3+u+1)\). Order its elements by coefficient vectors in the basis \(1,u,\ldots,u^7\), and let \(\theta\) be the first element satisfying \(\theta^{85},\theta^{51},\theta^{15}\ne1\); then \(\theta\) has order \(255\).

Use the recursive Garcia–Stichtenoth tower over \(K=\mathbb F_{16^2}\):
\[
F^{(1)}=K(x_1),\qquad x_{i+1}^{16}+x_{i+1}=\frac{x_i^{16}}{x_i^{15}+1}.
\]
At level eight choose the four completely split fibers above
\[
A=\{\theta,\theta^2,\theta^3,\theta^4\}.
\]
Order fibers by this displayed order and places inside each fiber lexicographically by their tuples of successive Artin–Schreier roots in the fixed polynomial basis. If \(E\) is their evaluation divisor and \(P_\infty\) is the unique pole of \(x_1\), define
\[
a=603,979,776,\qquad S_8=C_L(E,aP_\infty)\cap\mathbb F_2^{2^{30}}.
\]
There is no puncturing, shortening, repetition, or padding in this exact-length construction. The proof shows \(S_8=\{0,\mathbf1\}\).

The audited baseline trace route starts with an arbitrary binary code of length \(L=8,355,840\), repeats every coordinate \(128\) times, and appends exactly \(2^{22}=4,194,304\) zeros.
distance_audit: For the level-eight subfield code, \(\deg E=4\cdot16^7=2^{30}\) and \(a<\deg E\), so evaluation is injective.
Every nonzero \(f\in L(aP_\infty)\) has at most \(a\) zeros among the evaluation places. Hence every nonzero word of the subfield subcode has weight at least \(2^{30}-a=469,762,048\).
The exact calculation gives \(S_8=\{0,\mathbf1\}\), so its actual minimum distance is \(2^{30}\), stronger than the required distance.
For the repetition route, final weight is exactly \(128\) times raw weight; zero padding changes neither dimension nor weight. Thus the target forces raw distance \(469,762,048/128=3,670,016\).

The fixed-trace-list result concerns product-distance certification: every full-rank local trace encoder has inner distance at most \(64\). It does not exclude a proof exploiting correlations between symbol values at different coordinates.
For the intermediate \(\mathbb F_{16}\)-trace route, the bound \(2,105,916\) applies when distance is certified solely as inner minimum distance times \(\mathbb F_{16}\)-symbol distance.
explicitness_audit: The constant field, polynomial basis, primitive element selection, tower recursion, tower level, split fibers, divisor, and evaluation ordering are symbolically specified.
The selected elements are outside \(\mathbb F_{16}\): in the cyclic group \(K^\times\), an element \(\theta^i\) lies in \(\mathbb F_{16}^\times\) exactly when \(17\mid i\).
No graph, random sampling, search-selected codeword, or asymptotic hidden constant is used.
The exact level-eight construction uses four complete fibers and requires no length adjustment.
The baseline obstruction fixes both the 128-fold repetition and the final zero block of length \(2^{22}\).
No repository files were changed because this is a non-leaderboard obstruction result.

obstructions: Among unions of complete split \(x_1\)-fibers at one level of the recursive GS tower, exact length \(2^{30}\) is possible only at levels seven and eight. The corresponding binary subfield-subcode dimensions are at most \(73\) and \(9\).
For the specified four level-eight fibers, the subfield subcode collapses exactly to the repetition code \([2^{30},1,2^{30}]_2\).
Any binary code of raw length \(8,355,840\) completed by 128-fold repetition and the fixed zero padding has dimension at most \(1,015,831\) if it meets the target distance.

Every fixed full-rank list of 128 absolute-trace functionals on \(\mathbb F_{256}\) is merely a binary \([128,8]\) inner encoder, and Griesmer forces its distance to be at most \(64\), attained by \(\operatorname{RM}(1,7)\).

For \(\operatorname{Tr}_{256/16}(C)\) followed by the natural \([128,4,64]\) encoder, a symbol-distance/product proof permits at most \(526,479\) dimensions over \(\mathbb F_{16}\), hence at most \(2,105,916\) binary dimensions.
These statements do not rule out punctured non-fiber evaluation sets, special divisors, coordinate-varying low-pole trace multipliers, or a symbol-value-sensitive global weight proof.

proof_markdown:
### 1. Trace maps and the local Griesmer barrier

The absolute-trace pairing \((a,x)\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb F_2}(ax)\) is nondegenerate. Consequently every binary linear functional on \(K\) has the form \(x\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(ax)\), and every fixed list of 128 such functionals is simply a binary linear encoder
\[
\phi:K\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2^{128}.
\]
If the multipliers span \(K\), then \(\phi\) is injective and its image is a binary \([128,8,d_\phi]\) code. The [Griesmer bound](https://doi.org/10.1147/rd.45.0532) gives
\[
128\ge\sum_{i=0}^7\left\lceil\frac{d_\phi}{2^i}\right\rceil.
\]
For \(d_\phi=65\), the right side is
\[
65+33+17+9+5+3+2+1=135,
\]
so \(d_\phi\le64\). Thus a fixed full-rank multiple-trace list is exactly an ordinary inner code and cannot improve the \([128,8,64]\) product factor.

### 2. Direct binary trace followed by repetition

Let \(T\le\mathbb F_2^L\), where \(L=8,355,840\), and form
\[
\widehat T=\operatorname{Rep}_{128}(T)\oplus0^{2^{22}}.
\]
Every weight is multiplied exactly by \(128\), so the target requires
\[
d(T)\ge d_0=469,762,048/128=3,670,016=7\cdot2^{19}.
\]
The first twenty Griesmer terms sum to \(7(2^{20}-1)=7,340,025\); the next two are \(4\) and \(2\). Hence
\[
G_{22}(d_0)=7,340,031.
\]
All subsequent terms equal one. Therefore, for \(k\ge22\),
\[
L\ge7,340,031+(k-22),
\]
and consequently
\[
k\le1,015,831.
\]
The same conclusion is trivial when \(k<22\). This rules out every direct binary trace or subfield code completed by this repetition pattern.

For comparison, retuning the baseline divisor to \(\deg G=L-d_0=4,685,824\) gives outer dimension at least
\[
4,685,824+1-554,753=4,131,072.
\]
For any \(K\)-dimensional \(K\)-linear outer code, its binary trace has dimension at least \(K\): choose an information set of \(K\) coordinates, prescribe arbitrary trace bits there, choose field elements with those traces, and use surjectivity of the information projection. At binary dimension \(4,131,072\), direct Griesmer evaluation gives maximum possible distance \(2,112,389\): its first 22 terms sum to \(4,224,790\), and adding \(4,131,050\) unit terms gives exactly \(8,355,840\); increasing the distance by one increases the sum to \(8,355,841\). Thus the large trace dimension necessarily destroys the intended raw distance.

### 3. Complete split fibers in the recursive GS tower

By the [Garcia–Stichtenoth splitting theorem](https://doi.org/10.1006/jnth.1996.0147), each \(\alpha\notin\mathbb F_{16}\) gives a completely split fiber of size
\[
Q_m=16^{m-1}
\]
at level \(m\), and there are \(256-16=240\) available base fibers. A union of complete fibers has length \(N=2^{30}\) only if \(hQ_m=N\) with \(h\le240\). For \(m\le6\), one needs at least \(1024\) fibers; for \(m\ge9\), one fiber already exceeds \(N\). Thus only
\[
(m,h)=(7,64)\quad\text{or}\quad(8,4)
\]
are possible.

Let \(E\) be any such union and put
\[
w=\prod_{\alpha\in A}(x_1-\alpha).
\]
Complete splitting and total ramification give the exact principal divisor
\[
(w)=E-NP_\infty.
\]
Let
\[
U=\{f\in L(aP_\infty):\operatorname{ev}_E(f)\in\mathbb F_2^N\}.
\]
Because \(a<N\), evaluation identifies \(U\) with the binary subfield subcode. For \(f\in U\), the function \(f^2-f\) vanishes at every place in \(E\). Therefore
\[
\Psi(f)=\frac{f^2-f}{w}\in L((2a-N)P_\infty)=L(bP_\infty).
\]
The map \(\Psi\) is \(\mathbb F_2\)-linear and its kernel consists exactly of the two constant functions \(0,1\). Hence
\[
\dim_{\mathbb F_2}U\le1+8\ell(bP_\infty).
\tag{1}
\]

The exact semigroup recurrence of [Pellikaan–Stichtenoth–Torres](https://doi.org/10.1006/ffta.1998.0217) applies. At level seven, \(b=8\cdot16^6\) remains below every relevant conductor during recursive division, so
\[
H_7\cap[0,b]=\{j16^6:0\le j\le8\},\qquad \ell(bP_\infty)=9.
\]
At level eight, \(b=16^7/2\) is below the smallest positive nongap \(16^7\), so \(\ell(bP_\infty)=1\). Substitution in (1) gives the respective dimension caps \(73\) and \(9\).

### 4. Exact collapse for the specified level-eight fibers

Write \(Q=16^7\). Since \(a=(9/4)Q\), the same semigroup recurrence gives
\[
H_8\cap[0,a]=\{0,Q,2Q\}.
\]
As \(x_1\) has pole order \(Q\),
\[
L(aP_\infty)=\operatorname{span}_K\{1,x_1,x_1^2\}.
\]
Thus a binary evaluation word comes from
\[
p(X)=rX^2+sX+t
\]
with \(p(\alpha)\in\mathbb F_2\) for every \(\alpha\in A\). The polynomial \(p^2-p\) consequently has the four elements of \(A\) as roots.

If \(r\ne0\), degree and leading coefficient force
\[
p(X)^2-p(X)=r^2\prod_{\alpha\in A}(X-\alpha).
\]
The left side has zero \(X^3\)-coefficient. The coefficient on the right is
\[
r^2\sum_{\alpha\in A}\alpha
=r^2\theta(1+\theta+\theta^2+\theta^3)
=r^2\theta(\theta+1)^3\ne0,
\]
a contradiction. Hence \(r=0\). Now \(p^2-p\) has degree at most two and four distinct roots, so it vanishes identically. Coefficient comparison gives \(s=0\) and \(t\in\mathbb F_2\). Therefore
\[
S_8=\{0,\mathbf1\}=[N,1,N]_2.
\]

### 5. Intermediate-field product certificate

Let \(T=\operatorname{Tr}_{256/16}(C)\le\mathbb F_{16}^{L}\) have dimension \(r\) over \(\mathbb F_{16}\). Encode each symbol by \(\operatorname{RM}(1,3)=[8,4,4]_2\), repeat each binary coordinate sixteen times, and use the same final padding. This is an inner \([128,4,64]_2\) encoder. A proof using only symbol distance and inner minimum distance must establish
\[
d_{16}(T)\ge D/64=7,340,032=7\cdot16^5.
\]
The first six terms of the 16-ary Griesmer sum equal
\[
7,340,032+458,752+28,672+1,792+112+7=7,829,367,
\]
and later terms are one. Hence
\[
r\le L-7,829,367+6=526,479,
\]
so the resulting binary dimension is at most \(4r=2,105,916\).

These conclusions are deliberately scoped: the product arguments do not upper-bound an actual concatenated distance that exploits symbol values globally, and the full-fiber theorem does not cover punctured or non-principal evaluation sets.

research_direction: The surviving narrow route is an \(\mathbb F_{16}\)-trace code paired with the explicit \([128,4,68]_2\) local encoder. Crossing the ceiling requires an \(\mathbb F_{16}\)-linear trace code of length \(8,355,840\), dimension at least \(978,671\), and symbol distance at least \(6,908,266\); Griesmer permits dimension only up to \(987,027\). Certifying this window requires a new global trace-weight or simultaneous Artin–Schreier point-count argument. Fixed local trace lists, uniform repetition, ordinary product bounds, and complete split-fiber subfield subcodes cannot supply it.
theorem_statement: Let \(N=2^{30}\), \(D=7N/16\), and \(L=8,355,840\). In the recursive Garcia–Stichtenoth tower over \(\mathbb F_{256}\), an exact-length one-point binary subfield subcode \(C_L(E,(9N/16)P_\infty)\cap\mathbb F_2^N\), with \(E\) a union of complete split \(x_1\)-fibers, can occur only at levels seven or eight; its dimension is then at most 73 or 9, respectively. For the explicit level-eight fibers above \(\theta,\theta^2,\theta^3,\theta^4\), the code is exactly \(\{0,\mathbf1\}=[N,1,N]_2\). Independently, every binary length-\(L\) trace/subfield code completed by 128-fold repetition and \(2^{22}\) zero coordinates has dimension at most \(1,015,831\) if it meets distance \(D\). Finally, every fixed full-rank list of 128 absolute-trace functionals on \(\mathbb F_{256}\) is an ordinary \([128,8]\) inner code of distance at most 64. These are rigorous barriers for the stated natural alphabet-reduction mechanisms, not universal impossibility results for punctured, coordinate-varying, or globally analyzed trace constructions.
title: Frobenius-collapse and Griesmer barriers for GS alphabet reduction
